destinations.name: Statue of Liberty
destinations.description: The Statue of Liberty is a symbol of freedom and democracy. It was a gift from France to the United States and was dedicated in 1886. Visitors can take a ferry to Liberty Island to see the statue up close.
destinations.necessities: book tickets in advance, wear comfortable shoes

destinations.name: Central Park
destinations.description: Central Park is an 843-acre public park in the heart of Manhattan. It features several lakes, gardens, and walking paths. Visitors can rent bikes, take a boat ride, or simply relax in the park.
destinations.necessities: wear comfortable shoes, bring snacks and water

destinations.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
destinations.description: The Metropolitan Museum of Art is one of the world's largest and most famous museums. It features a vast collection of art and artifacts from around the world, including works by Monet, Van Gogh, and Vermeer. Visitors can spend hours exploring the museum's galleries and exhibitions.
destinations.necessities: book tickets in advance, wear comfortable shoes
destinations.search_query: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

destinations.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
destinations.description: The 9/11 Memorial & Museum is a tribute to the victims of the 9/11 attacks. The memorial features two large reflecting pools surrounded by the names of those who were killed. The museum tells the story of that day through artifacts and personal stories.
destinations.necessities: book tickets in advance, be prepared for emotional content

destinations.name: Top of the Rock Observation Deck
destinations.description: The Top of the Rock Observation Deck is a popular spot to take in the views of the city. Visitors can see the Empire State Building, the Chrysler Building, and other iconic landmarks from 70 floors up. It's a great spot to take photos and enjoy the sunset.
destinations.necessities: book tickets in advance, wear comfortable shoes
